correctness.rationale: The original definition requires each competitor to lie in the complement, to have exactly the same size, and to dominate the original Cartesian rook graph. A set dominates iff it meets every row or every column, since an unhit row and unhit column leave their intersection undominated. If 2k<=pq, a dominating k-subset in the complement would exist whenever all its rows or all its columns were met (choose one from each relevant class and extend), so accuracy forces D to contain a whole row AND a whole column. Conversely both full classes make every complement subset nondominating. If 2k>pq, no rival fits. Inclusion-exclusion over selected full rows/columns gives the claimed F_{p,q}; over omitted rows/columns gives B_{p,q}. Since 2(p+q-2)<=pq and the smallest full row+column union has p+q-1 cells, gamma_a=p+q-1. The exceptional minimum counts for p=2 and (3,3) follow from p+q-1>pq/2. Independently enumerated all graph-defined dominating rivals for every subset of the 2x2,2x3,2x4,2x5,3x3,3x4 boards and matched every polynomial coefficient. This is finite corroboration; the lemmas prove all p,q.
residual_risks: Finite enumeration covers six boards; the proof rather than enumeration supplies the unbounded-p,q quantifier.
The theorem concerns closed-neighborhood domination and equal-size complement rivals; different edge-domination conventions are excluded.

value.rationale: Rook graphs encode incidences of K_{p,q} and have a natural full-polynomial question. The formula counts every accurately dominating set at every cardinality, gives the first possible size and all minimum-level multiplicities including nontrivial exceptional boards. These are useful exact graph parameters, not merely a renamed general half-order lemma.
residual_risks: The high-half polynomial branch uses a known general observation; value rests materially in low-half classification and exceptions.
